Subject: Post-demo technical follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing, queues & SDK auth

Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo today. Good signal on expected workloads; looping in Lauren and Stephanie to confirm architecture details and make sure we capture a pragmatic dedicated capacity plan. Below is a concise recap plus action items so we’re all aligned.

Summary of your requirements (as stated on the call):
- Primary traffic: synchronous chat + short summarization (avg ~512 tokens request / 150 tokens response).
- Steady-state: ~120 requests/sec (QPS) during business hours; peak bursts up to ~400 QPS (3–4x) for promotional windows.
- Concurrency target: ~500 concurrent sessions (session = open chat with KV cache per user).
- Latency goal: p95 < 350ms for small-response paths, p95 < 800ms for longer summarization flows.
- Embeddings used for search & reranking: ~200k vectors initially; 5–10k embed ops/day, but batched nightly for indexing.
- Security: VPC + customer-managed KMS, SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Open technical questions for Redwood team (answered below where possible):
1) Autoscale policy triggers (queue depth vs GPU utilization) — what we recommend.
2) Recommended concurrency limits / per-GPU sizing for the models you want.
3) SDK auth patterns — service account vs API key for server-side calls.
4) Routing/fallback plan across model variants to meet latency SLOs.
5) Structured output / function-calling constraints for tool integrations (appointments & EHR lookups).
6) Embedding + reranker placement and typical throughput assumptions.

Attachments included: falkon-dedicated-sizing-worksheet.xlsx (fill this with your average payloads if useful). Also attached a short SDK snippet (sdk-auth-snippets.txt) for both API key and service-account flows.

Next steps / owners:
- Lauren: confirm per-GPU sizing and autoscale knobs, update worksheet -> target by EOD 2026-11-02.
- Stephanie: start SOC2 doc exchange (evidence list) and procurement intro; target 2026-11-04.
- Rafael: schedule technical TBD follow-up with infra (I’ll send a calendar invite once Lauren posts the sizing).

If I've missed anything, flag it — otherwise I’ll consider the sizing worksheet the single source for the capacity proposal.

Best,
Rafael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Rafael — this captures it well. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The 400 QPS peak is 10–15 minutes for campaign-driven loads; we'd rather overprovision burst capacity than throttle critical flows.
- For concurrency: when you say 500 concurrent sessions, is that per-region or global? We will route traffic primarily from US-east and US-west.
- Embeddings: initial vector set is 200k but will grow ~5% monthly. Reranker will be called on top-50 candidates from ANN.

Two asks before the sizing is finalized:
1) Can you confirm expected GPU instance types and per-GPU concurrency for the redwood-chat-v1 model and a quantized variant we discussed?
2) We will need a sample autoscale curve (simulated) that shows how queueing and latency behave when QPS spikes to 400 for 20 minutes.

Samir — looping you since procurement will want the SOC2 timeline.

Appreciate it,
Alex

Subject: Re: Post-demo technical follow-up: dedicated capacity sizing, queues & SDK auth

Alex — quick technical answers and a first-pass capacity model. Rafael, I uploaded the filled worksheet into the Drive link (see related_links).

1) Per-GPU sizing (first-pass):
- Model: redwood-chat-v1 (FP16 / quantized path): ~18 concurrent small-chat sessions per A100-80GB equivalent for p95 < 350ms at 512-token avg.
- For larger summarization requests (avg 662 tokens), expect 6–8 concurrent sessions per A100.
- Recommendation: mix of 6 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady state (120 QPS) + 6 additional GPUs as burst pool. That maps to ~144 small-chat concurrency capacity in steady and ~288 with burst pool active.

2) Autoscaling & queue behavior:
- We recommend a hybrid policy: primary trigger = GPU utilization > 72% sustained for 15s OR request queue length > 200 requests.
- Warm-up policy: scale one GPU increment per 30s; allocate burst-from-pool immediately for transient spikes < 10 minutes to avoid cold-start latency.
- For 400 QPS sustained for 20 minutes, simulation suggests p95 latency will rise to ~750ms if only steady pool exists; with burst pool engaged and warm-up policy, p95 stays under ~420ms. I will attach a simulated curve (worksheet tab: autoscale-sim).

3) Concurrency limits and queues:
- Per-worker concurrency cap: 32 in-flight token generation threads (internal to runtime) with per-connection semaphore to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Request-level queue: FIFO with priority bumping for health/heartbeat traffic. Backpressure returns 429 with Retry-After header; SDK will handle exponential backoff by default.

4) SDK auth:
- Server-to-server: recommend service-account JWT with short-lived keys + rotation through customer KMS for private deployments.
- For Hosted API: API keys with scoped permissions are acceptable; for your security posture we’ll provide mTLS option in Private deployment. See sdk-auth-snippets.txt (attached) for code samples.

5) Routing & fallbacks:
- Primary route -> redwood-chat-v1 (low-latency variant). Fallback chain: redwood-chat-tiny (quantized) -> redwood-chat-cpu (lower cost).
- Routing policy: prefer region-local GPUs; if region capacity < 30% available, route to sibling region with tenant-aware fallbacks.

6) Embeddings & reranker:
- Use redwood-embed-001 for indexing; batch nightly indexing to reduce peak embedding costs.
- Reranker: run reranker (rr-small-v1) only over top-50 ANN candidates. Expect 8–12ms per reranker call at scale (parallelized), plan concurrency accordingly.

I’ll update the worksheet with per-GPU numbers and a simulated autoscale curve by EOD.

—Lauren
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Quick procurement note — SOC2: we need a draft evidence list and expected time to handover. Stephanie, can you confirm the earliest date you can start the doc exchange? Also, two technical points:

1) Tool calling / structured output: our EHR integration will require strong schema validation and deterministic function-calling (no hallucinated field names). Does Redwood support schema-first function-calling with strict enforcement and canned error modes when the model output does not validate against schema?

2) Reranker throughput: if reranker is parallelized per-worker, will that consume additional GPU RAM or is it CPU-bound for rr-small-v1? We want to estimate cost for reranker-heavy flows (search in triage).

Alex / Samir — thanks for the quick follow-ups. Short answers and next steps (action-focused):

A) SOC2 evidence and procurement: Stephanie — can you start the evidence exchange on 2026-11-04? Samir, we’ll aim to have a draft pack within 7 business days.

B) Structured output / function-calling: yes — Redwood supports schema-first function-calling. Options: strict validation (reject outputs that fail schema, return structured error) or tolerant mode (attempt best-effort mapping + error token). For EHR flows we recommend strict mode + explicit canonical enums to avoid ambiguity. Lauren will add recommended schema templates to the Drive sizing sheet.

C) Reranker resource profile: rr-small-v1 is CPU-optimized for inference at top-50 scale; it can be pinned to CPU workers (recommended) to avoid consuming GPU capacity. If you pin to GPUs for extremely low-latency use-cases, expect ~10–15% additional GPU memory footprint (depending on batch size).

D) Commitment & timeline: we’ll prepare a dedicated capacity proposal (PDF) by 2026-11-05 that includes: per-GPU counts, burst pool sizing, autoscale triggers & simulation graphs, estimated monthly cost, SOC2 evidence timeline, and an integration checklist (SDK snippets, routing config, embeddings pipeline).

E) Meeting: propose a 45-min technical alignment on 2026-11-06 at 10:00 PST to go over the sizing PDF and confirm procurement milestones. I’ll send the invite once Stephanie confirms SOC2 start date.

Action owners (short):
- Lauren: finalize sizing worksheet & autoscale sim (due 2026-11-04).
- Stephanie: confirm SOC2 doc exchange start (due 2026-11-04).
- Rafael: deliver dedicated capacity proposal PDF (due 2026-11-05) + calendar invite for 2026-11-06.

Thanks — look forward to locking the plan.

Rafael
